name: Nationalism as extended egoism
plain_explanation: The romantic idea that a nation is like a large family or extended self -- a race descended from common ancestors sharing 'blood-consciousness' -- so that loving one's nation is really a projection of loving oneself.
precise_definition: The doctrine, exemplified by Mazzini, that nations possess a mystical corporate individuality and an absolute right to liberty, extending the romantic emphasis on blood-relation and self-projection from the family to the nation.
why_it_mattered: Russell presents it as the channel through which the essentially unpolitical romantic revolt against convention entered practical politics after the Revolution, becoming 'the most vigorous of revolutionary principles' in the earlier nineteenth century.
historical_origin: Develops out of the romantic emphasis on blood-relation (illustrated by Byron and Nietzsche) and reaches full political expression in Mazzini.
examples: Byron's advocacy of the principle of nationality
Association of belief in blood and race with anti-Semitism, illustrated by Byron's verse on 'Jew Rothschild'
influence_on_later_thinkers: Russell treats this strand as feeding into twentieth-century nationalism and, implicitly, fascism.
connection_to_politics_or_religion: Central political legacy of the chapter.
